steps.content: [Tuco - Street]

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I'm not even a slave... They're using me like cattle! Bastards!
As it turns out, Tuco does need extra hands desperately.
Hella follows Wright and toils nonstop from morning till night. Even during the occasional break, Korryn orders her to help out in the kitchen or clean the square.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Damn that bastard Korryn...
Hella grumbles quietly, but doesn't forget to keep an eye on her surroundings.
During her work hours, she searches nearly all of Tuco, and she still couldn't find a single trace of those stupid Hypercubes!
But... Hella looks ahead and spots Wright squatting and yawning in front of the little depot. A string of keys hangs from his waist, glimmering in the sunlight.
This little locked depot is the last spot she needs to investigate.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Mr. Wright, are we almost done organizing the big depot?

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Once these things are moved to the little depot, we're done. You go rest. I'll handle the rest.
The man waves his hand, motioning her to sit down.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: You've been working hard these past few days, Hella. Take a good rest after this. And if anyone asks, just say I let you. Even Korryn won't say a word!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: N-No need! I'm not that delicate!
It's definitely in that little room! Hella's eyes sparkle even brighter, putting on the look of an earnest, sweet girl.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Back when I was in Syndicate, I also did hard labor for food. I've been through it all. Don't worry about me.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: You've been helping me a lot these days, Mr. Wright. I want to help you in return.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Aww, what a sweet thing to say! That's really comforting to hear...
Wright takes out a ragged handkerchief from his pocket and dabs the corner of his eye.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: What a... what's the word for someone who says nice things? Oh right, what a chatterbox! What a tattletale! What a loudmouth!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Uh... Hehe. Th-thanks for the compliment...?
Thud! A lunchbox falls on Wright's head. It's Mira and little Timmy delivering food.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Just bear with it a bit longer. Next month, I'll get him a dictionary, but I can't guarantee he'll get things right.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You've been busy all morning. You must be hungry, right?
She opens the lunchbox, and the aroma of roasted meat wafts over.

steps.speaker: Timmy
steps.content: This one's for you, Mr. Wright. And Hella, this one's yours...
Hella takes the lunchbox, but little Timmy keeps holding onto the other end. He hesitates for a long time, then pulls something out of his pocket to place on top of the lunchbox.

steps.speaker: Timmy
steps.content: And this, this is for you too...!
It's two Hypercubes.

steps.speaker: Timmy
steps.content: It's... I learned how to make this dessert from Mira... and these are Hypercubes I got from three months of savings. It's not much, but I hope it helps...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Huh? For me?
Timmy nods gently.

steps.speaker: Timmy
steps.content: I want to apologize for what happened.

steps.speaker: Timmy
steps.content: The day the desert bandits came, you saved me. If it weren't for you, we wouldn't have been able to get rid of them so easily. But when the sandstorm came, we couldn't take you with us... and now...

steps.speaker: Timmy
steps.content: It's really, really great that you're okay...
Tears well up in his eyes. Hella quickly takes the lunchbox and stuffs the Hypercubes into her pocket.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hehe. It was just a few pesky bandits... nothing that would've killed me. Don't worry about it!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I accept your apology. Stop looking so sad. People at the market don't like doing business with cry babies...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: But this is all you were able to buy after three months of work? Are prices in WhiteSands that high?

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Yeah, Hypercubes are really expensive! Kiddo, if you want to make big money, you've got to hustle harder!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: If you want to grow tall, you should eat well and on time. You two as well. Don't forget to get some rest after all the work.
After that, Mira and little Timmy say their goodbyes and leave.
Hella finishes her lunch quickly and volunteers to clean the little depot. She uses sweet words like "the early bird catches the worm" and "kids clean faster" to make Wright unlock the depot door...
The little depot is not the splendid treasure trove that Hella had imagined. Amidst all the dust, there are just some old furniture and the big box that the Tuco folks had tried to flee with.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Huh? Why does that box look familiar...?

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Oh, that's the one we snatched from the desert bandits!
Just as expected! The Hypercubes are here!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: What a big box! There must be quite a few treasures in there, right?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: With the prices here, even if it's only half-filled with Hypercubes, it'll be enough to get you all to DisCity!

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Yeah right! I got to admit, we've really got lucky this time!

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: This box really does have good stuff inside. It's just a small bag that takes up less than a tenth of the box, but it's definitely something!

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Tuco has a lot of old folks and kids, but if we have this kind of luck a few more times, we won't have to worry about the next sandstorm at all. And I, for one, am always the luckiest in Tuco!
After a burst of proud laughter, the smile on his face fades a little. He looks at Hella with a complex expression.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: But no matter our situation, we really shouldn't have dragged a little girl like you into this.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Little Timmy said you're a good girl who helped us a lot, and you're just a child... Look at me. I'm a full-grown man, and not even as clear-headed as a kid. Silly me!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Mr. Wright, we're such close friends already. Do you really have to do all this bowing and apologizing, too?

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: It doesn't matter if we're friends or not, it's the right thing to do! You saved those Tuco folks and beat those desert bandits to a "pope." I have to thank you properly!
The middle-aged man who always misuses words rummages through his pocket and puts a paper-wrapped snack on her hand.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: But... the sandstorms are coming more frequently, and supplies are getting more expensive. Ultimately, it's because I haven't been a good sheriff for Tuco, otherwise Korryn wouldn't have to go out hunting for Hypercubes everywhere, and you wouldn't have been dragged into this.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Hella, if you want to blame someone, blame me! But Korryn is a good lass, so good... she's dragged down only because of our weakness.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Weakness...
The Syndicate girl lowers her head, looking at the snack on her hand.
The lunchboxes Mira sends are always filled to the brim. Abuela Susan specially wove her a sun hat, and Maggie nonchalantly "passes by" the depot with a cold drink at least three times a day.
As for Korryn... she sometimes suddenly pops up at her workplace, spooks her with Sheriff the Lizard, then leaves some snacks and disappears.
The wind lifts Hella's hair from behind and cools her hot, sticky neck.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...She's not weak at all. She's a big liar.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: I, Hella, trusted her with all my heart, but she deceived and used me. Revenge must be taken. I never forgive.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Haha, only half of what she says is true, and I'm the only one in town who can tell which half! I can tell Korryn really likes you...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Ah, enough!! Don't you know that no one likes sugarcoating? Enough of this topic!
A stronger gust of wind smacks the girl's back, making her stagger forward.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...! Why is the wind getting stronger? It's just like a few days ago...
She turns her head, and her complaint gets stuck in her throat.
On the horizon, a massive storm rolls in like a tidal wave, blotting out the sky.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Oh no! It's a sandstorm!
Dropping the lunchbox, Wright grabs Hella and starts running.

steps.speaker: Wright
steps.content: Go to the square! Meet up with the others!!
